Where each fragment is recorded

A fragment = one NLI Alma record (MMS). FGP inventory numbers were matched to MMS through the FGP image index and the catalogue's FGP field.

FGP database (FIST)

The Friedberg project's own database, restored from FIST_28_1_26.bak (28 Jan 2026) into a private SQL Server on the server. This is the data behind the FGP website: transcriptions, translations, bibliography, joins, identifications and condition.

FGP join types

Princeton Geniza Project enrichment

PGP's open data (github.com/princetongenizalab, pulled 10 Nov 2026) matched to our fragments by shelfmark. It adds transcriptions, translations, descriptions, dates and joins that are not on the server.

Sources & method

Source on the serverUsed for
/nas/archive/paris-data/metadata/transformed_catalogues/GNIZA_catalogue_from_marc_records.tsvNLI Geniza MARC catalogue (232,792 records): titles, languages, dates, physical description, condition, conservation, bibliography (581)
/nas/archive/FGP/FGP_all_data/fjms_part1/Genizah/info_Data.txtFGP image index (805,381 images, 227,559 MMS): FGP inventory, shelfmark, folders, Bavli/Rambam cross-listing
/nas/archive/FGP/FGP_all_data/Bibliography/581 הפניות ביב.xlsxFGP bibliography export, older than the FIST database (364,033 rows; 31,463 could not be linked to an inventory number); FIST counts are preferred where larger
/nas/archive/FGP/FGP_all_data/scans/GenizahScans.xlsxPrinted catalogues describing each fragment
/nas/archive/FGP/FGP_Geniza_transcriptions/altoHuman FGP transcriptions, ALTO XML (3,292 Rosetta IEs)
/nas/archive/FGP/FIST_DB_BACKUP/FIST_28_1_26.bak → private SQL Server 2022 (Developer) in /nas/archive/haifa-data/noam/mssqlFGP FIST database (Jan 2026): website counters (SnpShot.Inventory), transcriptions and translations with credits, bibliography with titles and authors, joins, identifications (textual frame), coded condition, script, material and copy dates. 236,833 FIST shelfmarks linked to 235,905 of our fragments via FGP inventory numbers and FIST's own Alma links; 21,574 FIST shelfmarks (1,602 with transcriptions) are outside our fragment set.
github.com/princetongenizalab/pgp-metadata, pgp-text (copy in .../fgp_report/pgp/)Princeton Geniza Project: documents, fragments, scholarship, transcription and translation texts. Matched by normalised shelfmark plus holding library; 34,086 of 37,023 PGP fragments matched (unmatched are mostly collections outside NLI/FGP, e.g. Dār al-Kutub, Princeton, Kaufmann).
/nas/archive/FGP/MultiFragmentsWithPartsMulti-part fragments
/nas/archive/paris-data/automatic_transcriptions/geniza/all_05_improved_rdg_order_CSVs/merged.tsv (38 GB)Kraken HTR on NLI images, summed per page and fragment
/nas/archive/paris-data/automatic_transcriptions/FGP_all_data/02-KRAKEN/ALTOs_converted_to_CSVs/merged.tsv (18 GB)Kraken HTR on FGP images
/nas/archive/paris-data/metadata/LISTs/, .../duplicates/NLI_GNIZAImage counts on the server; records sharing identical images
Caveats.
  • "Studied" relies on the bibliography recorded by NLI/FGP. Research not entered there is invisible, so these are lower bounds.
  • Published transcription and translation come from the tags FGP adds to each reference ("יש העתקה", "יש תרגום", "(מלא)/(חלקי)").
  • Condition and material are free-text detections and are only as complete as the catalogue.
  • Dates exist for only about 5% of records.
  • The NLI "Geniza" set also includes some full codices, e.g. Firkovich items in St. Petersburg. They are flagged is_codex_like.
  • Snapshot dates. The NLI catalogue export stops in May 2024; the FGP database is from 28 Jan 2026; PGP was pulled on 10 Nov 2026. Anything added to the FGP website after January 2026 is not included.
  • Only FGP records shown on the public FGP site are used: the public counters, and references marked "not for publication" or "for allowed users only" are excluded.

Scripts and intermediate files: /nas/archive/haifa-data/noam/fgp_report/ (build.py, hum.py, analyze.py, htr_agg.sh). The CSV is UTF-8 with BOM, so it opens correctly in Excel. A Parquet copy is next to it on the server.
